title: Smooth surjective algebraic spaces have etale local sections
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $T$ be an $S$-scheme, $V$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $p:V\to T$ a smooth surjective morphism. Smooth means smooth on etale scheme charts, with scheme smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]; surjectivity means surjective on field-valued point classes, where two field-valued maps are equivalent if they agree after pullback to a common field extension. There exist a set-indexed family of schemes $T_i$, etale morphisms $e_i:T_i\to T$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] whose images cover $T$, and maps $v_i:T_i\to V$ such that $p v_i=e_i$ for every $i$. All these objects and maps lie within the chosen big site. The empty target is allowed, with its empty covering.

source.place: Tag 0CFV (lemma-etale-dominates-smooth), applied to the singleton smooth covering V over T; its proof reduces to more-morphisms.tex Tag 055V (lemma-etale-dominates-smooth).

proof.text: If $T$ is empty, take the empty family. Its union of images is $T$, and all lifting conditions are vacuous. Hence assume $T$ is nonempty.

Apply [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover] to $V$ to obtain a scheme $W$ and a representable surjective etale map $a:h_W\to V$, with $|a|$ surjective on field-valued point classes. Put $q=p\circ a:W\to T$. By the stated chart meaning of smoothness of $p$, this scheme morphism $q$ is smooth. Also $|q|=|p|\circ|a|$ is surjective: for each $t\in|T|$ first choose a point class of $V$ above $t$ using the hypothesis on $p$, then a point of $W$ above that class using the cited surjectivity. Thus $q$ is a smooth surjective morphism of schemes.

source.place: Tag 0CFV (lemma-etale-dominates-smooth), proof: replace the source by a surjective etale scheme atlas. Point-surjectivity made explicit using spaces-properties.tex Tag 03FX (lemma-cover-by-union-affines).

proof.text: Apply [sbc-lem-slicing] to the smooth scheme morphism $q:W\to T$. Obtain an etale covering $b_i:U_i\to W$ and factorizations $q b_i=e_i r_i$, where $r_i:U_i\to T_i$ has a section $s_i:T_i\to U_i$ and $e_i:T_i\to T$ is etale. No condition on the characteristic, separation, quasi-compactness or Noetherianity is required by the cited statement.

source.place: Tag 0EY4 (lemma-cover-smooth-by-special), used for the scheme-refinement step of spaces-topologies.tex Tag 0CFV instead of introducing a duplicate of the local-section consequence of Tags 055U and 055V.

proof.text: Define $v_i=a b_i s_i:T_i\to V$. Then $p v_i=q b_i s_i=e_i r_i s_i=e_i$, since $r_i s_i=\mathrm{id}_{T_i}$. Given $t\in|T|$, choose $w\in|W|$ with $q(w)=t$ by step 2, and choose $u\in|U_i|$ with $b_i(u)=w$ by the covering in step 3. Then $e_i(r_i(u))=t$, so the images of the $e_i$ cover $T$. Use the set of indices of that covering, and representatives in the chosen bounded site as in [def-weil-size-convention]; the atlas and scheme slicing are taken in those same universes. This gives the required set-indexed family and all the asserted factorizations.

source.place: Tag 0CFV (lemma-etale-dominates-smooth), final refinement argument; section composition and coverage written out for the Tag 0EY4 factorizations.

lean.statement: theorem exists_etale_local_sections {S : Scheme.{u}} (V : AlgebraicSpace S) (T : Over S) (p : V.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hp : SpaceMapIsSmooth V T p) (hsurj : pointImage p = Set.univ) : ∃ (I : Type u) (Tᵢ : I → Over S) (e : ∀ i : I, Tᵢ i ⟶ T) (v : ∀ i : I, yoneda.obj (Tᵢ i) ⟶ V.obj.obj), (∀ i : I, Etale (e i).left) ∧ (∀ t : T.left, ∃ (i : I) (tᵢ : (Tᵢ i).left), (e i).left.base tᵢ = t) ∧ (∀ i : I, v i ≫ p = yoneda.map (e i))
